# Next parent action: stop note for task 3, no dispatch

**Why the loop stops here**

- The ordinary CR loop is exhausted. Review 3 returned `FIX_FIRST` with `TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING`, so the convergence exception did not apply and the rule was "escalate".
- The one escalated round has already been used. Its fix ran on `<configured-impl-model>` and its CR re-review ran. That re-review is still `FIX_FIRST`, with residual `src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard`.
- Per `reference/fix-loop.md`, any escalated-round review that still has issues ends in a stop note per `stop-note.md`, with no second dispatch.
- The restored `**Amend-grant:** fund 2 fix rounds` does not authorize a dispatch on this resume:
  - The transcript has no recoverable funded-round lines for task 3, so I cannot establish how much of the grant, if any, is unspent.
  - The token was not newly written or refunded on resume.
  - The funded-round dispatch rules are not in the text I have, and I will not reconstruct them.
  - So no funded round goes out. I also add no spent carrier and change no handoff/resume grammar.

**State held at the stop**

- No shell commands run. In particular:
  - no `git add -A`
  - no new Fix delta tree capture (no re-review is being dispatched)
  - no `reset --soft "$WAVE_BASE_SHA"` and no wave commit
- `/workspace/project` stays as-is, with the integrated, uncommitted wave plus repairs. The review source stays `BASE_SHA: <WAVE_BASE_SHA>`, `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE` for any later re-review.
- No `plan_tracker` write. Task 3 stays `in_progress` and the phase stays `implement`. No further tasks or waves start.
- The commit happens only after a later CR `SHIP`. It would be the step-7 fold, followed by marking task 3 `complete`.

**Reply (inline; the turn ends after this)**

```
Stopped on task 3 (Validate frame); escalated round on <configured-impl-model> did not resolve it.

Problem: the frame validator still reads the frame without checking its length first, so a short frame is not rejected before use.
  src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard

Fix options:
  a) add a length guard at src/frame.ts:21 that rejects a frame shorter than the minimum the spec defines, before any field read
  b) amend plan task 3 (or the spec section it anchors) to state the exact length precondition and expected rejection, so the guard has an unambiguous target
  c) fund more fix rounds for task 3: reply with a fresh grant in the existing form, e.g. `**Amend-grant:** fund 2 fix rounds`; the restored grant is not reused because no record of its spent rounds survived the resume

Pick one, or give another fix.
```

**How the human refunds funding:** reply with a newly written grant using the existing `**Amend-grant:** fund N fix rounds` form. Because that grant is written in a live turn, it is unambiguous funding for task 3. The restored token from before the resume is not that.

On such a reply, I would dispatch the funded fix as a plain in-place `implementer` in `/workspace/project`. The payload would carry:
- the final CR report verbatim
- the task 3 full text, spec anchors and status protocol
- `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test frame.test.mjs`

After it, I would stage with `git -C /workspace/project add -A`, record the Fix delta tree, and send a CR-only re-review. It is CR-only because `Behaviour-change: no`. The re-review would carry `## Previous review report (re-review trigger)`, the trajectory block, `## Fix delta`, `BASE_SHA: <WAVE_BASE_SHA>`, and `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE`.
